tools.name: create_work_item
tools.title: Create Work Item
tools.description: Create an open Work Item in explicit project_id. For manual work provide caption and optional description; for a tracker ticket provide provider and external_id (ticket ID, key or supported URL), and the server reads the tracker text. Requires at least two project environments only when inserting. An existing ticket returns created=false without overwriting text/status/project; a ticket in another project returns ticket_project_mismatch. Manual creation is not idempotent: inspect list_work_items after an uncertain response before repeating.

tools.name: update_work_item
tools.title: Update Work Item
tools.description: Update caption and/or description of a Work Item in explicit project_id; send only changed fields. Uses the product update RPC with force=false by default. Ticket-linked text returns tracker_fields_readonly; unlink_ticket=true alone clears the ticket reference and retains the text, then edit in another call. force=true is an explicit override and does not grant permissions. Does not archive, move projects or change group/deployment links.

tools.name: archive_work_item
tools.title: Archive Work Item
tools.description: Archive a Work Item in explicit project_id. Already archived is a no-op. Active group membership returns group_operation_required: leave the group explicitly in the UI first. Does not delete the card or detach deployments. Restore with unarchive_work_item.

tools.name: unarchive_work_item
tools.title: Restore Work Item
tools.description: Explicitly restore an archived Work Item in project_id to open. Already open is a no-op. Does not create a deployment or run and does not require project readiness for the existing card.

tools.name: link_work_item_deployment
tools.title: Link Work Item Deployment
tools.description: Attach an existing deployment to an open Work Item. Pass project_id, work_item_id and deployment_id explicitly. Same-team visibility and user edit permission apply. Uses the product link RPC and preserves group rules; an assembled group deployment belongs to its master. Returns linked=true and changed (false if already linked). Does not change saved config, create a run or deploy metadata. Inspect get_work_item afterward: attaching a deployment with successful past runs can change the displayed delivery state. work_item_links_changed requires refreshing and confirming again, not blind retry; work_item_link_superseded preserves the historical carrier.

tools.name: unlink_work_item_deployment
tools.title: Unlink Work Item Deployment
tools.description: Remove the association between a Work Item and an existing deployment. Pass project_id, work_item_id and deployment_id explicitly. Returns linked=false and changed (false if already absent). Does not delete the deployment, cancel a run or roll back Salesforce; its runs stop contributing through this link to the card delivery state. A locked group returns group_operation_required: use the explicit group operation in the MTDT UI; never automatically unlock or detach group members. work_item_links_changed requires refreshing and confirming again, not blind retry.

tools.name: preview_work_item_promotion
tools.title: Preview Work Item Promotion
tools.description: Preview promotion using the existing MTDT product operation, without creating a draft or run. Pass explicit project_id, work_item_id and from_environment_id. The server derives the next environment and donors; returns the product verdict, blockers/pending deployments, existing carriers, full fold (components, smart overrides and deletions), delta options, scope_fingerprint and optional group stack/version. A green board cell is not promotion approval. Review the result before create_work_item_promotion; reopen reuses an existing draft, not a new create.

tools.name: create_work_item_promotion
tools.title: Create Work Item Promotion Draft
tools.description: Create a promotion DRAFT through the existing product operation, never a validation or real deployment run. Pass the same project/item/from_environment IDs and scope_fingerprint from preview_work_item_promotion. Defaults to full; delta is a restriction of preview full fold and requires delta_allowed. Explicit supersede replaces open drafts in full mode only; review supersedable/carriers first, never replace a delivered carrier. For a group pass stack_version from preview; the product requires full assembly. Stale scope/stack and all product refusals are preserved. Returns deployment_id (also product id), to_environment_id, mode and optional superseded/supersede_failed: when an ID exists, keep it even if a replacement failed, never blindly repeat creation. Product links may include other cards sharing donor content; inspect the resulting cards/links. Read the saved draft, preview_deployment_run, then validate/deploy by ID separately.

scope_fingerprint.description: Opaque fingerprint returned by preview_work_item_promotion; pass unchanged.

supersede.description: Explicit open draft IDs to replace. Full mode only; use preview.supersedable after reviewing replacement.

stack_version.description: For a group, pass preview.stack.version unchanged; group promotion requires full mode.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.title: List Projects
tools.description: List every project visible to the current user, optionally within team_id. Returns project id, team_id, caption and description. Discover project_id here and pass it explicitly to all project tools, even when only one project exists. Does not select or remember a current project.

tools.name: list_project_environments
tools.title: List Project Environments
tools.description: Read a project and its complete environment chain ordered by position, including org IDs, names and kinds. project_id is required. work_items_ready means at least two environments are configured; reads of existing Work Items remain available in unconfigured projects.

tools.name: list_work_items
tools.title: List Work Items
tools.description: List ALL non-archived Work Items of the explicitly supplied project_id, without a hidden result limit. Set status=archived or all to include archived items. Includes active group/master context and computed delivery: reached/current/next environments, validation, rollback markers, drafts/runs, Done and linked deployment summaries. Uses the same rules as the UI. group_delivery separately describes a member master; own delivery does not silently inherit master history. Readiness is advisory, not promotion approval. Does not create tasks or change data.

tools.name: get_work_item
tools.title: Get Work Item
tools.description: Read one Work Item within an explicitly supplied project_id, including text, tracker reference, active group/master context and computed delivery plus linked deployment summaries. work_item_id alone does not infer the project. Archived items are readable; deleted or inaccessible items are not found. Validation is not delivery; rollback retains the UI historical presence marker. current_environment may be the first working environment even when reached_environment is null. group_delivery separately describes the master history, when applicable. Does not mutate data.

tools.name: list_orgs
tools.title: List Salesforce Orgs
tools.description: List the Salesforce orgs connected to the user's team(s). Returns id, label, instance_url, derived org_type (scratch/sandbox/developer/production), is_important (protected org), namespace and reauth_required. Use this to find the org id for a deployment source/target.

team_id.description: Optional team ID. If omitted, lists orgs across all of the user's teams.

tools.name: resolve_target
tools.title: Resolve Target Org
tools.description: Resolve a free-text org name (e.g. "QA") to candidate connected orgs, ranked by match score. Returns the top candidates with id/label/instance_url/org_type/is_important so you can confirm the right one before using it as a deploy target — do not assume the top hit; confirm, especially if a production org is among the candidates.

query.description: Free-text org name to resolve, e.g. "QA", "acme prod". Matched against org label and instance URL.

team_id.description: Optional team ID to scope the search. If omitted, searches all of the user's teams.

tools.name: list_deployments
tools.title: List Deployments
tools.description: Find an existing deployment without creating one. For deployments linked to a Work Item, list_work_items/get_work_item also return deployment IDs. Lists the team's deployments newest-first with source (org / git repo / metadata backup / metadata set, each labelled), target (label + org_type + is_important so you can tell a production target apart), and the LATEST run's status (status, is_terminal, is_success, is_validation, is_rollback). `has_description` tells you whether the deployment already has a release note (the text itself is not listed — it can be kilobytes of HTML); set or replace it with set_deployment_description. Each row carries owner.id + owner.is_you so you can tell your own work from a teammate's (owner.label is only filled for your own deploys — other users' display names are not readable under row-level security). Use it to answer "did yesterday's release land?", "what went to this org recently?", or to resume work after losing context; filter with org_id (+ org_role="target" for deployments INTO an org) and created_since/created_until. Org-comparison objects are excluded by default.

team_id.description: Optional team ID. If omitted, lists across all of the user's teams.

org_id.description: Optional org ID filter — only deployments involving this org.

org_role.description: How org_id must be involved: "target" = deployments INTO that org (default "either").

include_comparisons.description: Include org-comparison objects (is_comparison rows), which are not deployments. Default false.

created_since.description: ISO date/datetime — only deployments created on/after it (e.g. "what went out this week").

created_until.description: ISO date/datetime — only deployments created on/before it. Pair with created_since for a release window.

limit.description: Max deployments to return, newest first (default 20, capped at 50).

tools.name: get_deploy_status
tools.title: Get Deploy Status
tools.description: Get an INSTANT snapshot of the latest run of a deployment by its id. Returns a derived status, whether it is terminal/succeeded, whether it was a validation, component/test failure details, counts, folder_sharing_check advisory findings from the final package, and the SF validation job id (for quick-deploy). To WAIT for a run to finish, prefer await_deploy_status (it blocks server-side up to ~50s per call, collapsing the poll loop). If you poll this tool manually instead, poll every 15–30s — not faster — to avoid burning the tools/call rate limit.

deployment_id.description: Deployment ID (metadata_deploys.id) to get the latest run status for.

tools.name: await_deploy_status
tools.title: Await Deploy Status
tools.description: Wait for a deployment run to reach a terminal state, server-side. Blocks up to ~50s per call (default/cap) polling internally, then returns the same payload as get_deploy_status the moment is_terminal becomes true. If it has not finished within the window it returns the latest status with timed_out=true and a hint — just call await_deploy_status again to keep waiting (repeat while timed_out=true). A not-yet-created run (status "no_run") is treated as non-terminal and waited on. Read-only; never throws on timeout. Use this instead of a manual get_deploy_status poll loop.

deployment_id.description: Deployment ID (metadata_deploys.id) to wait on the latest run of.

timeout_s.description: Max seconds to wait server-side (default 50, capped at 50).

tools.name: create_deployment
tools.title: Create Deployment
tools.description: Create a deployment between source and target. Optionally pass project_id plus work_item_ids to attach existing open cards in the same call. A late link failure returns error=work_item_link_failed with deploymentId and confirmed/unconfirmed IDs: the deployment EXISTS, so inspect it and finish linking in the UI; do not repeat creation. Source can be an org, repo, metadata backup, or archive. Exactly one of from_org_id, from_repo_id, from_backup_id, or from_archive_id must be specified. Target must be an org. An archive source is unpacked in the background and ALL its components get selected: wait with check_deployment_creation_status until "done", then preflight_deployment / recommend_tests / validate_deployment by deployment_id. Optionally pass caption (short title) and description (release note — its plain text becomes the git commit message on a push-to-git deploy and is appended to approval requests); the description can be changed later with set_deployment_description. A backup source must be a FINISHED backup that has an archive — otherwise it returns { error:"backup_not_usable", reason } and creates NO deployment.

project_id.description: Required together with work_item_ids. All cards must belong to this project and team.

work_item_ids.description: Work Items to attach during creation; omit to create an independent deployment.

from_archive_id.description: Source archive ID (from register_archive or list_archives). Every component of the archive is selected automatically.

caption.description: Short title for the deployment (shown in lists).

description.description: Longer description / release note for the deployment. Plain text or HTML. Its plain text becomes the git commit message on a push-to-git deploy and is appended to approval requests. Change it later with set_deployment_description.

deploymentId.description: The created deployment id, including a partial link failure. Never repeat creation when this ID is present.

error.description: A business refusal, or work_item_link_failed after creation. backup_not_usable and Work Item preflight refusals create no deployment.

linked_work_item_ids.description: Work Item links confirmed by the server.

unconfirmed_work_item_ids.description: Links requiring inspection after a late failure; a network error can hide a committed link.

backup.description: { id, label, status, partial, has_archive } of the rejected backup.

tools.name: set_deployment_description
tools.title: Set Deployment Description
tools.description: Set or replace a deployment's description after it was created (pass an empty string to clear it). Plain text or HTML — the Deploy modal renders it as rich text, turns its plain text into the git commit message for a push-to-git deploy, and appends it to approval requests, so this is the deploy's release note rather than a private comment. Use caption for a short title instead. Returns the saved value.

deployment_id.description: Deployment ID whose description to set.

description.description: The new description. Plain text or HTML. Pass an empty string to clear it.

tools.name: check_deployment_creation_status
tools.title: Check Deployment Creation Status
tools.description: Is the deployment populated and ready to browse? Returns the overall deploymentStatus ("done" | "in progress" | "failed") PLUS each side (source/target) with its raw populated value, its kind (org/repo/backup/metadata_set) and the population task behind it { id, task_type, status, error } — so a failed source unpack next to a finished target is reported as "failed" with the Salesforce/storage error, not as an endless "in progress". Needed before browse_metadata on repo/backup sources; org sides populate lazily and are fine to browse right away. "failed" will not change by polling: for a backup source edit the deployment and pick a finished backup that has an archive, or create a new deployment; for an org side re-authenticate it and press Refresh in the web app.

deploymentStatus.description: Overall verdict: "done" (both sides populated), "failed" (either side failed — this deployment will not populate), "in progress".

source.description: { state, populated (raw column, e.g. "in progress (unpacking)"), kind: org|repo|backup|metadata_set, task: { id, task_type, status, error, created_at } | null }

target.description: Same shape for the target side.

tools.name: prepare_deployment_run_selected_items_object
tools.title: Prepare Deployment Run Selected Items
tools.description: LOW-LEVEL normalization only; does not save or launch. Prefer add_deployment_components to save the selection before validate_deployment: normalize an { metadata_type: [base_component, …] } map into the selected-items object a deployment run needs. Metadata types are soft-resolved (autofixes common wrong guesses like "ApexClass"→classes; rejects made-up types with suggestions). If any type is unresolvable it returns { error, unresolved } and NO selectedItems — fix the types and retry.

deployment_id.description: Deployment ID — when set, the metadata-type resolver also matches types already retrieved for this deployment.

error.description: Set to "unresolved_types" when some metadata types could not be resolved.

tools.name: create_deployment_run
tools.title: Create Deployment Run (Validate or Deploy)
tools.description: Run the deployment using its FULL saved config (components, overrides, partial selections and deletions). Pass deploy_id, optionally validate and execution options; never pass items or config. Save composition first with add_deployment_components/remove_deployment_components, inspect it with get_deployment_components. Returns task_id; wait with await_deploy_status.

validate.description: Run in validation mode (checkOnly) instead of a real deploy. To later quick_deploy this run, validate with a test_option that runs tests.

comment.description: Optional comment (shown on approval requests / audit).

test_option.description: Apex test level. "local" runs org+package tests (required if you intend to quick_deploy afterwards); "relevant" lets Salesforce select tests automatically; "specific" needs tests_to_run; "NoTestRun" fails on production targets.

tests_to_run.description: Comma-separated Apex test class names. Only used when test_option="specific".

do_package_backup.description: Enable the "Metadata Backup" — captures a pre-deploy snapshot of the target so this run can be rolled back later.

objects_to_backup.description: Object API names to snapshot record data for before deploying (record backup).

request_approval.description: Request approval instead of deploying directly (forced by the server when the user lacks direct-deploy on the target).

tools.name: preview_deployment_run
tools.title: Preview Deployment Run
tools.description: Preview a validation/deployment WITHOUT creating tasks, saving settings or calling Salesforce. Reads the saved config and applies the same optional execution options as launch. Returns component counts, deletions, test level, backups, Apex code, git push, jobs, activations and all remaining execution settings. Flow activation comes only from the saved deployment. validate defaults to false (real-deploy plan); use true before validate_deployment. Review actions with the user before launch, using the same options. Draft/settings may change before launch; permissions, approval and worker checks are not guaranteed by preview.

validate.description: Run in validation mode (checkOnly) instead of a real deploy. To later quick_deploy this run, validate with a test_option that runs tests.

backup.description: Alias for do_package_backup when previewing validate_deployment with backup.

comment.description: Optional comment (shown on approval requests / audit).

test_option.description: Apex test level. "local" runs org+package tests (required if you intend to quick_deploy afterwards); "relevant" lets Salesforce select tests automatically; "specific" needs tests_to_run; "NoTestRun" fails on production targets.

tests_to_run.description: Comma-separated Apex test class names. Only used when test_option="specific".

do_package_backup.description: Enable the "Metadata Backup" — captures a pre-deploy snapshot of the target so this run can be rolled back later.

objects_to_backup.description: Object API names to snapshot record data for before deploying (record backup).

request_approval.description: Request approval instead of deploying directly (forced by the server when the user lacks direct-deploy on the target).

tools.name: quick_deploy
tools.title: Quick Deploy (No Test Re-run)
tools.description: Deploy a package that a previous validation already compiled and tested, WITHOUT re-running tests. Only works after a Succeeded validation that ran tests. Pass just deployment_id to auto-derive the validation job — this performs a REAL deployment to the target org. This returns immediately; then call await_deploy_status to wait for it to finish (repeat while timed_out=true), or use get_deploy_status for an instant snapshot.

deployment_id.description: Deployment ID whose successful validation to quick-deploy.

quick_deploy_job_id.description: Optional: the Salesforce validation job id. Omit to auto-derive from the latest successful validation of this deploy.

source_validation_task.description: Optional: the metadata_deploy_results.id of the validation run. Omit to auto-derive.

scheduled_at.description: Optional ISO datetime to defer the deploy. Omit to deploy now.

request_approval.description: Request approval instead of deploying directly.

tools.name: preflight_deployment
tools.title: Preflight Deployment Checks
tools.description: Run the pre-deploy checks the Deploy UI runs automatically for a human, and get them as one normalized list — call it before validate_deployment / quick_deploy. Checks: folder_sharing (report/dashboard folder recipients missing on the target, or explicit target grants removed or downgraded by the outgoing folder XML), destructive_impact (deleting something the target still references), permissions_and_profiles (which profiles/permission sets grant access to what you are shipping), record_backups (objects whose RECORDS should be backed up first), cron_triggers (scheduled Apex that blocks overwriting a class), business_hours (Entitlement Process whose Business Hours is missing on the target — SF reports success and silently drops the binding), non_source_deployable (types no source deploy can carry between orgs because the body embeds an org-bound id — ship them as a package instead), static_analysis (effective, post-suppression findings of the latest scan), changed_since_donor (combined deployments only: components a donor deployment delivered that the source org has touched since — the deploy ships the body the source org has now and Salesforce reports success either way). Returns { checks, verdicts, counts, pending }: each verdict has severity ("warning" | "info"), what is affected, and often a suggested_action. ADVISORY — nothing here blocks a deploy, exactly like the UI. Checks that query the target org can be slow: anything that did not finish inside the budget comes back in `pending` — call again with checks:[...] to collect just those, or pass depth:"fast" for the DB-only subset. For a deployment created from an archive pass all_items:true instead of items to check every component of the archive.

items.description: Optional explicit components for an advisory check, keyed by type → names. Omit items/all_items to check the full saved deployment config.

all_items.description: Deployment created from an archive only: check every component of the archive instead of naming them in items.

destructive_items.description: Components you intend to DELETE on the target, same shape. Enables the destructive-impact check.

destructive_changes_is_post.description: Destructive timing: false deletes before deployment, true deletes afterwards.

depth.description: "fast" runs only DB-backed checks (sub-second); "full" (default) also runs the checks that query the target org.

checks.description: Run only these checks. Omit to run all.
Per-check status: ok | found | skipped | timed_out | error.

pending.description: Checks that ran out of budget — call again to collect them.

advisory.description: Always true: preflight never blocks a deploy.

error.description: "unresolved_types", "unknown_checks", "checks_incompatible_with_depth", or with all_items "archive_not_ready" / "archive_unpack_failed" / "all_items_not_supported" / "archive_empty"; "missing_selection" / "conflicting_selection" when items and all_items are both absent or both set.

incompatible_checks.description: Valid check ids excluded by the depth filter — re-run with depth:"full".

tools.name: run_impact_analysis
tools.title: Run Impact Analysis
tools.description: Given the metadata you intend to deploy, find what else on the source org it depends on that you should probably add too. Returns dependency findings that each map back to a selectable {type, base_component}. Read-only and synchronous — pass the selectedItems object you would deploy.

selected.description: The items you intend to deploy, keyed by type → [{ base_component }] (the selectedItems object from prepare_deployment_run_selected_items_object).

deep_scan_mode.description: Scan depth. Default "jit_only" (fast, uses already-retrieved metadata).

tools.name: check_target_conflicts
tools.title: Check Target Org Conflicts
tools.description: Check whether any item you are about to overwrite or delete on the TARGET org has changed since it was last retrieved (i.e. someone edited the target after your snapshot). Returns honest verifiable vs not-verifiable buckets with reasons. Read-only. Run before a deploy to a shared org.

selected.description: Items to deploy (overwrite on target), keyed by type → [{ base_component }].

destructive_changes.description: Items to delete on target, same shape.

tools.name: recommend_tests
tools.title: Recommend Apex Tests
tools.description: Recommend which Apex tests to run for a selection (from class naming + code references, 2 hops). Pass items { type: [names] } to assess exactly that selection; omit items to assess the saved deployment selection, falling back to the latest run only for a legacy deployment without saved selection. Returns {recommendation, testsToRun, uncovered, unresolved, byComponent, reason, caveats, selection_source: "items"|"all_items"|"latest_run"|"deployment_config"|"none"}; "NoApex" with selection_source "none" means nothing was selected anywhere — pass items. Feed testsToRun into validate_deployment with test_option="specific". For a deployment created from an archive pass all_items:true: the tests are picked from the archive's own test classes (packageSource "archive"), so call it before validating. Read-only.

items.description: Optional components to assess, keyed by type → names. Omit to assess the saved deployment selection; legacy deployments without saved selection fall back to the latest run.

all_items.description: Deployment created from an archive only: assess every component of the archive instead of naming them in items.

tools.name: get_task_status
tools.title: Get Task Status
tools.description: Get task status by task ID (works for any async task: deployment runs, backups, comparisons, retrievals).

tools.name: get_workflow_deployment_recipe
tools.title: Get Workflow Deployment Recipe
tools.description: Return a recommended workflow for deploying recently changed classes.

tools.name: start_full_metadata_deployment_comparison
tools.title: Start Full Metadata Comparison
tools.description: Start a full metadata deployment comparison for a deployment.

tools.name: get_full_metadata_deployment_comparison_status
tools.title: Get Metadata Comparison Status
tools.description: Get status for a full metadata deployment comparison task.

comparison_id.description: Full metadata deployment comparison task ID.

tools.name: get_latest_full_metadata_deployment_comparison
tools.title: Get Latest Metadata Comparison
tools.description: Get latest full metadata deployment comparison for a deployment. Each row carries metadata_deploy_id; poll live status with get_full_metadata_deployment_comparison_status(comparison_id) using the comparisonId that start_full_metadata_deployment_comparison returned — the ids inside these rows are comparison-internal, NOT task ids.

tools.name: run_metadata_backup
tools.title: Run Metadata Backup
tools.description: Run a metadata backup for an org. Track it with get_task_status(task_id).

task_id.description: The backup task id — pass to get_task_status.

tools.name: list_metadata_backups
tools.title: List Metadata Backups
tools.description: List metadata backups of an org that can serve as a deployment source (status done AND an archive present) — newest first, with a human label (caption or 'backup <date> (<status>)'). Pass include_unusable:true to also see unfinished/no-archive backups, each with unusable_reason. Reads the 60 newest backups and returns at most 20: `count` is the number of rows returned, `hidden_unusable` the number of unusable rows filtered out of those 60. Use a returned id as from_backup_id in create_deployment.

include_unusable.description: Also return backups that cannot serve as a deploy source (unfinished, or done but with no stored archive). Default false.

tools.name: list_git_repos
tools.title: List Git Repositories
tools.description: List git repos for a team.

tools.name: list_archives
tools.title: List Archives
tools.description: List uploaded metadata archives (zip files on the Archives page) of the user's team(s), newest first: id, caption, description preview, created_at, size_in_bytes, origin (upload / mcp_upload / deployment_change_set / …) and, for archives registered over MCP, component_count + types. Use an id as from_archive_id in create_deployment.

team_id.description: Optional team ID. If omitted, lists archives across all of the user's teams.

name_contains.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on the archive caption.

limit.description: Max archives to return, newest first (default 20, capped at 50).

tools.name: request_archive_upload
tools.title: Request Archive Upload Link
tools.description: Step 1 of deploying a zip you have locally (SFDX source format — force-app/… with or without sfdx-project.json — or Metadata API format with package.xml). Returns { path, upload_url, curl }: run the curl command in your shell with the zip path filled in — the file goes straight to mtdt storage and never passes through this conversation. Then call register_archive with the same team_id and path. The link is short-lived (expires_in_seconds — can be as little as 2 minutes), so have the zip ready BEFORE calling this and run the curl command right away; if it expired, call request_archive_upload again. Max 50 MB. Needs a shell that can run curl. If you have no shell, do not try to send the zip contents through tool calls: ask the user to upload the zip on the Archives page of the mtdt web app (then find it with list_archives), or to push the project to a connected git repo and deploy from the repo.

team_id.description: Team that will own the archive.

file_name.description: File name of the zip, e.g. "release-42.zip".

path.description: Pass to register_archive after the upload.

upload_url.description: Signed upload URL, valid until expires_at.

expires_in_seconds.description: Lifetime of the upload link — run the curl command before it runs out.

tools.name: register_archive
tools.title: Register Uploaded Archive
tools.description: Step 2 after request_archive_upload: turns the uploaded zip into an archive. SFDX source is converted to Metadata API format; the archive appears on the Archives page. Returns { archive_id, component_count, types } — counts only, no file contents. Rejects: "not_uploaded" (the curl upload has not happened or failed — rerun it, or request a new link if it expired), "invalid_archive" (neither SFDX source nor a Metadata API package), "archive_empty", "too_large". Then create_deployment with from_archive_id = archive_id.

team_id.description: Same team ID as in request_archive_upload.

caption.description: Archive title shown on the Archives page. Defaults to the file name.

description.description: Optional longer description of the archive.

archive_id.description: Success: pass as from_archive_id to create_deployment.

error.description: "not_uploaded", "too_large", "invalid_archive", "archive_empty", "forbidden" or "invalid_request" on a reject; NO archive is created.

tools.name: browse_metadata
tools.title: Browse Metadata
tools.description: THE way to see what metadata a deployment can deploy. Browse the components of ONE metadata type on the deployment's SOURCE side (org, git repo, or metadata backup — resolved automatically from the deployment; pass org_id only to browse a specific org side, e.g. the target). Optional server-side filters: name_contains / modified_since / modified_by. Returns one row per COMPONENT { name, type, last_modified, last_modified_by }, most-recently-modified first, paginated (page / page_size; total is the full component count). For org sources, uncached metadata is retrieved on first call with a short poll (~15s): while the retrieval is still running it returns { status:"retrieving", partial:true, components (the partial set so far), task_ids } — just call browse_metadata again with the same args (idempotent, dedupe-safe) until status:"ready" (0 components is a valid ready). Treat the list as complete only at status:"ready". If the retrieval fails on the Salesforce side for part of the type you get { status:"retrieval_failed", failed_tasks:[{id,status,error}], components }: the component NAMES are complete, some bodies may not have been read yet. mtdt retries the retrieval automatically (up to 3 times) — call browse_metadata again to get the list; if the failure keeps repeating, report the error to the user. Repo/backup sources are populated when the deployment is created (see check_deployment_creation_status). Unknown types return a structured reject with did_you_mean suggestions.

metadata_type.description: Metadata type to browse, e.g. "classes" ("ApexClass" is fuzzy-resolved). One type per call (mirrors the wizard).

org_id.description: Org to browse. Defaults to the deployment's SOURCE org.

name_contains.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on the component name.

modified_since.description: ISO date; keep only components whose properties.lastModifiedDate is on/after this.

modified_by.description: Keep only components last modified by one of these names (properties.lastModifiedByName).

status.description: "ready" (the retrieval finished — components is the complete set; also returned with 0 components when the type simply has no metadata in this org, see hint), "retrieving" (still running — components is a PARTIAL set so far, call again) or "retrieval_failed" (a JIT task failed/cancelled for part of the type; see failed_tasks — mtdt retries automatically, call again).

components.description: One row per COMPONENT { name, type, last_modified, last_modified_by }, most-recently-modified first. On retrieving/retrieval_failed the list is partial (more may still arrive).

total.description: Component count matching the filters (across all pages). While status="retrieving" it grows as more components arrive.

partial.description: True when components is an incomplete snapshot (status="retrieving") — call again until status="ready" before treating the list as the full set.

task_ids.description: Retrieving: the JIT task ids still running.

failed_tasks.description: retrieval_failed: [{ id, status, error }] per failed JIT task — error is the Salesforce-side reason. mtdt re-queues the retrieval automatically (up to 3 times); report the error only if it keeps repeating.

tools.name: validate_deployment
tools.title: Validate Deployment (Check-Only)
tools.description: Validate the deployment using its FULL saved config (checkOnly, never a real deploy). Pass deployment_id and optional test/backup/comment settings only. Save components first with add_deployment_components; get_deployment_components shows the saved composition. Existing overrides, partial selections and deletions are preserved. Archive components are selected automatically after population; wait for check_deployment_creation_status. Returns task_id/status validating, or an actionable reject without creating a task. Wait with await_deploy_status.

test_option.description: Apex test level. Omit to use the saved testOption, or local if none is saved. Inspect preview_deployment_run first. Tests must run to enable quick_deploy. "relevant" lets Salesforce select tests automatically; "specific" needs tests_to_run; "NoTestRun" fails on production targets.

tests_to_run.description: Comma-separated Apex test class names. Only used when test_option="specific".

backup.description: Enable the pre-deploy "Metadata Backup" so a later real deploy of this run can be rolled back.

comment.description: Optional comment (shown on approval requests / audit).

task_id.description: Started: the validation run task id (scalar from the RPC) — pass to get_task_status / await_deploy_status.

error.description: "unresolved_types" or "items_not_retrieved" on a structured reject; with all_items "archive_not_ready" / "archive_unpack_failed" / "all_items_not_supported" / "archive_empty"; "missing_selection" / "conflicting_selection" when items and all_items are both absent or both set.

component_count.description: all_items: number of components sent to validation. Can exceed register_archive component_count: an object whose fields are shipped is sent as its own component too.

tools.name: get_deployment_components
tools.title: Get Saved Deployment Components
tools.description: Read the deployment saved composition: selected components, deletions, manual overrides and partial selections. The UI and MCP run this same saved config.

tools.name: add_deployment_components
tools.title: Add Deployment Components
tools.description: Add full source components to the saved deployment config. items is {metadata_type:[names]}; types are normalized and source components must be retrieved (browse_metadata). Repeating an add is a no-op. Other saved config is preserved. Manual overrides are preserved and do not block selection edits; edit their contents in MTDT. Components with partial selections must be edited in MTDT.

tools.name: remove_deployment_components
tools.title: Remove Deployment Components
tools.description: Remove full components from the saved deployment selection; does not delete them from Salesforce. Other config, including deletions and overrides, is preserved. Manual overrides are preserved and do not block selection edits; edit their contents in MTDT. Components with partial selections must be edited in MTDT.
